newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican peso weakens on sharp fall in Cetes rate.
newsitem.headline: Mexican peso weakens on sharp fall in Cetes rate.

text.p: The Mexican peso opened weaker against the dollar on Wednesday across the board following Tuesday night's sharp fall in primary interest rates, traders said.
"To begin with, some banks are letting pressure mount in the market, using interest rate levels as a pretext," a trader said.
"But pressure on the peso may ease in a bit, because there are foreigners waiting in the wings for better prices to buy pesos," he added.
The benchmark 48-hour spot peso opened 1.6 centavos weaker at 7.5650/7.5710 per dollar, and its 24-hour counterpart 1.45 centavos weaker at 7.5625/7.5675 per dollar.
The same-day peso meanwhile opened 2.95 pesos weaker at 7.5600/7.5625 per dollar.

Bellwether 28-day Cetes rates fell by much more than the market was expecting at Tuesday night's primary auction, plummeting 201 basis points from the prior auction to 23.46 percent. Traders surveyed by Reuters had been expecting a fall of 141 basis points.
"One positive aspect of the primary auction was the heavy demand for paper, and a substantial part of it from foreigners," a peso trader said.
Traders estimated that the spot peso could fluctuate between 7.55 and 7.57 per dollar on Wednesday.
